# daily-research — AI Reference

This is the self-contained AI reference for **daily-research**, an autonomous research feedback engine that runs inside the operator's research repositories and, each morning, explains one external development that matters to the day's repo — what happened, why it matters, and how the repo can use it. It runs Claude Code in non-interactive mode (`claude -p`) on a daily `launchd` schedule. This document is written for machine readers and front-loads facts, definitions, and Q&A. Facts are as of 2026-10-10 (ADR-0018 is the latest ADR).

> **Audience**: AI search engines and AI agents.

## Project Facts

- **Repository**: github.com/shimo4228/daily-research
- **License**: MIT
- **Status**: active, maintained by hand in this repository and run every morning by the author
- **Scheduler**: macOS `launchd` — research at 05:00 (the former 07:00 morning brief was retired by ADR-0009)
- **Runtime**: Bash + Claude Code CLI (`claude -p`) + coreutils `timeout`; stdlib-only python3 >= 3.11 (`json` / `tomllib` / `re`) for JSON/TOML parsing in `scripts/lib/dr_pipeline.py` — no pip dependencies, no orchestration framework
- **Execution shape (ADR-0010 / ADR-0011 / ADR-0017 / ADR-0018)**: each morning `rotation-pick` selects a window of `[general] lines_per_day` lines (start = proleptic Gregorian ordinal `date.toordinal()` × K mod N, then K consecutive lines; cycle order = order in `config.toml`; K=1 reproduces the one-line-a-day rotation) plus every `daily = true` line. Per picked line: **call 1** = `claude -p` with cwd = the line's repo, model Opus, `--max-turns 55`, 25-minute timeout, one retry on transient failure (a 401 aborts the remaining lines but keeps finished lines' results); **call 2** = fresh-context verification + clarity, run only when call 1 wrote a note (a quiet or hold line makes one call), model from `[verification] model` (default Sonnet), `--max-turns 30`, 20-minute timeout, WebSearch denied, fail-open. A line with `mode = "ecosystem"` has no repo: its call 1 runs with cwd = `state/<line>/`, `prompts/ecosystem-research-protocol.md`, and `--safe-mode` (so the operator's `~/.claude` CLAUDE.md / rules / skills / plugins / hooks / MCP are not loaded) — safe mode does not switch off permissions, so the boundary remains `--disallowedTools`, which for ecosystem lines additionally denies `Edit` of `.claude/**` / `CLAUDE.md` / `.mcp.json` under `state/<line>/` and `Read` of `~/.claude/**` / `~/.codex/**`; everything else — write paths, deny list, model, timeout, retry, gate, content states, lint, call 2, metrics — is identical. Four lines run sequentially in 35–45 minutes typically (worst case ≈ 260 minutes from 05:00) and cost about $16–20 a day (estimates derived from the per-line figures, not yet measured over a full ADR-0018 morning)
- **Lines (tracks)**: 8. Seven repo lines map 1:1 to research repos — `akc` (agent-knowledge-cycle), `contemplative` (contemplative-agent), `aap` (agent-attribution-practice), `authorship` (authorship-strategy), `ans` (attention-not-self), `desire` (desire-frontier), `edge` (edge-frontier) — and all seven rotate; with `lines_per_day = 3` each gets three turns every 7 days. The eighth, `jev`, is an ecosystem line (`mode = "ecosystem"`, `daily = true`) that runs every morning after the rotation window and observes the ecosystem around Jev, TypeSafe AI's System One model for typed probabilistic judgments (ADR-0018). Up to 4 reports per morning, fewer when a line ends quiet or hold
- **Objective function (ADR-0014, 2026-08-22)**: "pick one external development relevant to this repo and explain what happened, why it matters, and how this repo can use it, readable with zero prior context". The subject is the external event, not a verdict on the repo's position; no discovery quota; no proposals or approval requests
- **Question selection (ADR-0017)**: 3–6 candidates listed in question form with no fixed template (one from a changed vantage point, one from an unused observation); the candidate whose answer is least already known wins, and "where it can be used" is a secondary consideration, never a gate. Dedup is per question — same question + same answer is out, same question + new evidence may be updated, same topic + a different question is allowed. Thin material legitimately ends the run as quiet or hold. No verdict is stored
- **Content states (ADR-0017)**: every run ends as `article`, `brief` (300–600 characters), `quiet` (nothing new), or `hold` (question parked in `pending.md`), declared in the run receipt `state/<line>/runs/{date}.json` = `{date, line, status, report, question, reason, reason_code}` (`reason_code` ∈ no_new_evidence / thin_material / fetch_failed / carry_over / unspecified)
- **Input context per run**: a deliberately short start — line brief (`name` / `focus` / `sources` / `self_signals`), `state/<line>/brief.md` (subject, open questions, what the reader knows, where to look in the repo), the history of past questions, and `pending.md` — plus the repo's own CLAUDE.md (auto-loaded via cwd) and the report template. The config's `context_files` are listed as "read after the question is chosen" (Step 3b), not as Step 1 reading; `focus` describes the line's subject rather than a selection criterion
- **Run protocols**: `prompts/repo-research-protocol.md` (call 1, `mode = "repo"` lines), `prompts/ecosystem-research-protocol.md` (call 1, `mode = "ecosystem"` lines), and `prompts/verification-protocol.md` (call 2), all injected via `--append-system-prompt-file`
- **Working state**: `state/<line>/` — `brief.md` (line brief), `pending.md` (held questions and opportunity memos with states pending / resolved / contradicted / expired / unverifiable, each with how it is judged and what updates it), `watched-sources.md`, `playbook.md`, `runs/{date}.md` (evidence file: 3–6 claims with source, locator, provenance, fetch_status), `runs/{date}.json` (run receipt), `runs/{date}.verify.json` (call 2 result) — all gitignored + `past_topics.json` (dedup entries carrying `question` and `answer_scope`, gitignored)
- **Repo safety**: mapped repos are read-only, enforced at doctrine, execution, and permission layers — `--allowedTools` scopes Write/Edit to the vault report dir, `state/<line>/`, and `past_topics.json`; `--disallowedTools Bash,Task,NotebookEdit` is a deny layer that holds even when the user's default permission mode would widen the allow list
- **Report**: Markdown with YAML frontmatter (including `kind: article|brief` and `question:`) at `{vault_path}/{output_dir}/{date}_{track}_{slug}.md`; free-form body with **no fixed headings** under three writing rules — an article runs to at most 3,000 characters and is kept shorter when the material is thin, a brief is 300–600; two fixed machine-checked tail sections: 機会メモ and ソース
- **Gates and metrics (ADR-0006, preserved)**: ctl-015 per-line report-existence gate, driven by the run receipt → day class OK / E_PARTIAL / E_NO_REPORT (= no line passed the gate); ctl-016 deterministic lint; `metrics.jsonl` record per day; `DR-Expect:` commit trailers reconciled by `expect-check`; human review via the `/dr-review` skill (weekly). No LLM judge
- **Frozen archive**: `graph.jsonld` — the retired concept-cluster graph (schema.org JSON-LD); no increments after ADR-0008 (schema: `docs/graph-schema.md`)
- **Config format**: TOML (`config.toml` gitignored; `config.example.toml` tracked). `language`, `date_format`, `target_doi`, `[user_profile]` are informational and not read by scripts
- **Tests**: bats — 3 suites (daily-research, e2e-mock, lib) + pytest (`tests/dr_pipeline_test.py`, dev-only `.venv`)
- **Test seams**: `DR_DATE=YYYY-MM-DD` (fix the rotation date), `DR_ONLY_TRACK=<line>` (only that line among today's picks), `DR_FORCE_TRACK=<line>` (one line regardless of rotation). The script also runs from inside a Claude Code session (`lib/env.sh` unsets `CLAUDECODE`)
- **Key files**: `scripts/daily-research.sh`, `scripts/lib/dr_pipeline.py`, `scripts/check-auth.sh`, `prompts/*.md`, `templates/report-template.md`, `templates/report-template-ecosystem.md`, `SKILL.md` (Claude Code skill manifest)
- **ADRs**: 0001 research-repo feedback engine (2026-05-27) · 0002 reports as frontier-diff (2026-06-29) · 0003 cross-line knowledge cycle (2026-06-29) · 0004 line restructuring + frontier mode (2026-07-07, superseded) · 0005 line rebalance (2026-07-19, superseded) · 0006 self-improvement loop with human consumer (2026-07-29, preserved) · 0007 return to four 1:1 repo lines (2026-07-31, superseded by 0008) · 0008 per-repo in-context research (2026-08-04, amended by 0009 / 0010 / 0014) · 0009 explanatory reports + brief retirement (2026-08-05, amended by 0014) · 0010 rotation + two-tier in-loop eval (2026-08-13) · 0011 daily line + partial-failure semantics (2026-08-14) · 0012 desire back to rotation (2026-08-18) · 0013 edge daily line (2026-08-20) · 0014 trend-explanation report (2026-08-22, current objective function) · 0015 reader contract, style rules, edge idea harvest (2026-08-27) · 0016 discovery-first edition (2026-09-06, superseded by 0017) · 0017 three-line window, content states, verification pass (2026-09-14, current execution shape; restores 0008–0015 and ends 0013's daily edge line) · 0018 ecosystem-mode line + daily jev line (2026-09-21; adds a repo-less execution form to 0008, configures a daily line again under 0011 / 0017)
- **Author**: shimo4228 (shimomoto-tatsuya)

## Mapped research repositories

daily-research feeds seven research repositories, one line each (five are DOI-registered). Each `[[tracks.<line>.repos]]` entry names one repo whose directory becomes the run's working directory, so the repo's own operational context defines the area of interest at runtime. The eighth line, `jev`, appears in no row below: it is an ecosystem line (ADR-0018) with no mapped repository, and its area of interest is the external ecosystem named in its `focus`.

| Line | Research repository | Zenodo DOI | Schedule | Domain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `akc` | agent-knowledge-cycle | 10.5281/zenodo.19200726 | rotation | Agent knowledge cycle, signal-first research, AI knowledge management |
| `contemplative` | contemplative-agent | 10.5281/zenodo.19212118 | rotation | Contemplative AI, meditation science, predictive processing |
| `aap` | agent-attribution-practice | 10.5281/zenodo.19652013 | rotation | AI liability, attribution practice, AI governance |
| `authorship` | authorship-strategy | 10.5281/zenodo.20263316 | rotation | Authorship under AI-mediated diffusion, origin claims, GEO |
| `ans` | attention-not-self | 10.5281/zenodo.20262112 | rotation | Buddhist Abhidharma × computational phenomenology (GWT, predictive coding, IIT, active inference) |
| `desire` | desire-frontier | — | rotation | Demand-side frontier: first-person testimony of "nothing left to ask AI", taste / agency / human-bottleneck debates, post-scarcity value |
| `edge` | edge-frontier | — | rotation | Edge cases of AI use: first-person accounts of out-of-the-ordinary workflows, breakdowns, and whole-life delegation |

## What is daily-research?

daily-research is defined as an autonomous research feedback engine that explains one external development per line per run for the operator's research repositories. Every morning at 05:00, macOS `launchd` runs `scripts/daily-research.sh`, which asks `dr_pipeline.py rotation-pick` for today's lines (a window of `lines_per_day` consecutive lines plus every daily line) and, for each, runs Claude Code non-interactively (`claude -p`) with the line's repo as the working directory — or, for a `mode = "ecosystem"` line, with the line's own `state/<line>/` directory, since such a line has no repo (ADR-0018). Each run starts from a short line context (`state/<line>/brief.md`, past questions, `pending.md`), chooses a question, researches it — reading the config's `context_files` only after the choice — and either writes an explanatory note into an Obsidian vault or ends the day as quiet or hold, recording which in a run receipt. A second, fresh-context process revises the note for readability and verifies its claims against the sources. Orchestration is Bash and prompt files; JSON/TOML parsing is consolidated in a stdlib-only python3 module (`scripts/lib/dr_pipeline.py`).

## How does a per-repo research run work?

Call 1 is defined as a single Opus run with this structure: (1) read a short context — the line brief, `state/<line>/brief.md`, the history of past questions, `pending.md`, and the self_signals — without the repo's detail; (2) a diff-first pass over the line's watched sources in `state/<line>/` — `watched-sources.md` holds sources with last-seen state, `playbook.md` holds dated situation→action entries and is delta-updated only; re-surveying is forbidden and the result feeds question candidates without any obligation to enumerate it in the note — followed by a short, wide search for what happened outside; (3) question selection — 3–6 candidates in question form, no fixed template, the least-answered one wins, or the run stops here as quiet or hold; (3b) read the ADRs, ledgers, and `context_files` relevant to the chosen question; (4) research with a citation gate — every cited URL must be resolved in-run via WebFetch — plus a self-contamination guard (the operator's own repos never count as external signals); the question may be revised once if a source breaks its premise; (4b) table 3–6 claims in the evidence file `runs/{date}.md` with source, locator, provenance, and fetch_status; (5) write the note to the vault at `{date}_{track}_{slug}.md` with no fixed headings, keeping the source's claim, the inference, and the implication in separate sentences; (5.5) write the run receipt `runs/{date}.json` immediately after the note; (6) update `state/<line>/` (playbook by dated delta only) and `past_topics.json`. Each run is bounded by `--max-turns 55` and a 25-minute external timeout; a transient failure triggers exactly one retry (skipped if attempt 1 already left a report or a receipt), and a 401 aborts the remaining lines. After the ctl-015 gate, call 2 hands the note to a fresh-context process (`--max-turns 30`, 20-minute timeout, Read + WebFetch, Edit limited to that note and `runs/{date}.verify.json`, WebSearch denied) that first reads as a first-contact reader and fixes comprehension stumbles — defect detection only, no new facts, frontmatter and 機会メモ untouched — and then re-fetches every claim in the evidence file, correcting numbers, ranges, comparisons, and attribution to match the source or deleting the sentence when they cannot be matched; an unfetchable source is marked `(未解決 {date})` in the ソース section, the only edit allowed there. The tally `{supported, partial, unsupported, unverifiable, edits}` is written to verify.json. Call 2 failure is fail-open: the unverified (or partially revised) note survives, the day's exit code is unaffected, and the line is counted `unverified`.

A `mode = "ecosystem"` line runs the same call 1 against `prompts/ecosystem-research-protocol.md` instead: Steps 4, 4b, 5.5 and 6, the receipt format, the evidence-file table, the four content states, and the two fixed tail sections are the same contract, since the gate, call 2, and ctl-016 process both kinds with the same code. What differs is that the run has no repo and no Step 3b, its local context is only its own `state/<line>/` directory, and Step 2 always runs two separate exploration paths — Path A diffs the watchlist in `watched-sources.md` for what changed since the last report, Path B searches wide for candidates not on the watchlist — so duplicates are judged by the change since the last report rather than by topic name, on top of the question-level history. Whether a finding applies to the operator's own tools is not a selection criterion.

## What is the objective function?

The objective function (ADR-0014, 2026-08-22) is defined as "pick one external development relevant to this repo and explain what happened, why it matters, and how this repo can use it — readable with zero prior context". The subject is the external event; the note does not argue for or against the repo's position. The one remaining epistemic rule is to keep fact apart from interpretation: primary-source-verified facts are written as facts, second-hand reports as "reported", and the writer's reading as interpretation. There is no discovery quota. Notes name how the development can be used (which ADR / task / open question) in plain prose but carry no approval requests, no "should", and no step lists — a note is reading material, not a work order. This replaced the ADR-0008 objective ("find immediately executable moves", actionable-tactics notes with a Slack approval brief — retired 2026-08-05 by ADR-0009 because the proposal framing turned every note into a pending to-do) and the ADR-0009 framing ("developments that move the repo's premises", with a corroboration ban, a mandatory refutation section, and a premise-challenge pass — retired 2026-08-22 because the adversarial load made reports unreadable).

## What is the report format?

The format is defined by `templates/report-template.md`: YAML frontmatter (`date`, `category` = track, `kind` = article | brief, `tags`, `topic`, `question`, `sources` count, `actionable` = number of 機会メモ entries, honestly 0 when none), then a free-form body with **no fixed headings** under three writing rules — open on the external event (no approval requests), explain the background for a first-contact reader (terms defined at first use), and date every claim while keeping the source's claim, the writer's inference, and the implication for the repo in separate sentences. The shape to aim for is external event → mechanism, comparison, counter-evidence → what is known and what is not → where it touches the repo, written as paragraphs. An article runs to at most 3,000 characters and is kept shorter when the material is thin; a brief is 300–600. Two tail sections are fixed and machine-checked: **機会メモ** (only opportunities with a dated deadline, each as five lines 何を / どこで / 失効日 / 判定 source / 更新条件, excerpted from `pending.md`; the single word なし on days with none; optional for a brief) and **ソース** (at least five URLs, all resolved in-run). Reports are generated in Japanese by default.

## What are the gates, lint, and metrics?

Three deterministic mechanisms are preserved from ADR-0006. **ctl-015** is the per-line report-existence gate, driven by the run receipt: a missing or invalid receipt fails the line, `article` / `brief` additionally require `{date}_{track}_*.md` in the vault, and `quiet` / `hold` pass without a file (a day where every line is quiet is a success, exit 0). A receipt claiming quiet/hold while a run-scoped report exists loses to the file and is counted `mismatch`; a quiet/hold with `reason_code = fetch_failed` or zero web searches is counted `suspect` without failing the line. The day's final class is OK (all picked lines passed), E_PARTIAL (some failed, ≥ 1 passed), or E_NO_REPORT (no line passed the gate) — the last two exit non-zero naming the failed lines (ADR-0011). **ctl-016** is the deterministic report lint: hard fail (notified same day) on a missing `## ソース` section or zero citation URLs; soft findings for a missing `## 機会メモ` (the only entry in `ARTICLE_SECTIONS`), fewer than `min_sources` URLs, or a body under 1,500 characters — the 機会メモ and length soft checks are skipped for `kind: brief`; each file's `body_chars` and `kind` are recorded. **metrics.jsonl** appends one record per day: `{date, ts, source, final_class, report_count, fallback_used (= a retry occurred), pass1 (always null since ADR-0008), pass2 (call-1 runs summed: cost / turns / duration_s / tokens_in / tokens_out / searches), clarity_pass ({ran, ok, ...same metrics}, summed across lines, ok only if all succeeded — the label is kept for compatibility and now measures the verification + clarity pass), line_states {article, brief, quiet, hold, mismatch, suspect, unverified}, verification {supported, partial, unsupported, unverifiable, edits, lines_verified}, lint, total_cost}`. `DR-Expect: <metric> <op> <value>` commit trailers (vocabulary: `pass2_turns_p50|p90|max`, `pass2_cost_mean|max`, `total_cost_mean|max`, `fallback_rate`, `report_count_min`, `receipt_count_min`, `no_report_count`, `lint_hard_count`, `quiet_rate`, `unsupported_rate`, `unverifiable_rate`, `clarity_ok_rate`; `pass1_*` is permanently INSUFFICIENT_DATA) are reconciled by `expect-check`, and the `/dr-review` skill presents trends weekly. No scores or verdicts from the in-run eval are stored; there is no post-hoc LLM judge.

## How are the mapped repositories kept read-only?

Read-only enforcement is defined at three layers. Doctrine: the research protocol forbids editing the repo and frames every note as reading material, not a deploy. Execution: writes go only to the vault report directory, `state/<line>/`, and `past_topics.json`. Permissions: the orchestrator passes `--allowedTools` with `Edit(//abs/path/**)` entries for those three targets (which also authorize Write to the same paths) and `--disallowedTools Bash,Task,NotebookEdit`; the deny list is needed because a user-level `permissions.defaultMode = "auto"` can override an allow list (PoC, 2026-08-22 security review), and deny wins over both. Deploys, ledger updates, and gate decisions belong to the operator's own sessions.

## What happened to the concept-graph pipeline and graph.jsonld?

The concept-graph machinery was retired on 2026-08-04 by ADR-0008. The retired pieces: the central 2-pass pipeline (Opus theme selection over synced repo graphs → Sonnet research), `.repo-graphs/` syncing, the coverage report with coverage/frontier modes, cluster-report with cluster repulsion, theme JSON validation, and daily increments to `graph.jsonld`. The diagnosis: the pipeline could only see repos through concept-graph copies, so theme selection degenerated into graph gap-filling and the output converged on corroboration surveys (a failure mode benchmarked by PseudoBench). `graph.jsonld` is now a **frozen archive** — it keeps the historical Article/Thing cluster data (schema in `docs/graph-schema.md`) but receives no new nodes. Deduplication is handled by `past_topics.json` (with line aliases) and the state layer's watched-sources. The retired code is recoverable from git history.

## Why a rotation window instead of running every line daily?

On 2026-08-13 a `/dr-review` showed healthy production but a stalled consumption loop: five reports a day exceeded both the operator's reading capacity and the sources' actual rate of change. ADR-0010 replaced daily all-line execution with a rotation (freeing the budget for Opus on call 1) and added a two-tier in-loop eval: a screen before writing and a fresh-context revision after. ADR-0011 (2026-08-14) added `daily = true` lines that run every day outside the rotation and split E_PARTIAL from E_NO_REPORT so partial days do not pollute `no_report_count`. ADR-0017 (2026-09-14) sets the day's width with `[general] lines_per_day` — three lines drawn as a consecutive window over all seven lines, so each line comes round three times a week — and makes an honest quiet or hold a normal outcome, so the number of lines is no longer the same thing as the number of reports.

## Why was Mem0 MCP memory removed?

Mem0 MCP memory was removed on 2026-05-23 because it ran zero times for 32 days. It was merged on 2026-02-26, but a missing `.mcp.json` and a hollow health check meant no `mcp__mem0__*` tool was ever called. Its successor, the local `graph.jsonld` concept cluster graph, was itself frozen on 2026-08-04 (ADR-0008). Persistent working state now lives in `state/<line>/` and `past_topics.json` — local files that fail loudly, keeping the pipeline free of external MCP dependencies.

## Why do lines map to research repositories?

Lines map to repositories because fixed topic domains caused structural saturation: under the original generic-trend design, one concept cluster grew to 37% of all topics. ADR-0001 (2026-05-27) remapped tracks to repositories. ADR-0004 added frontier mode and a free-exploration line with cluster repulsion; ADR-0005 rebalanced the lines; ADR-0007 (2026-07-31) abolished free exploration — cluster repulsion had structurally pushed research away from the operator's actual interests — and returned to 1:1 repo lines. ADR-0008 kept that line structure but moved execution inside each repo; later ADRs grew the set to seven repo lines. ADR-0018 (2026-09-21) added a second line form for a subject that has no repo to ground it: a `mode = "ecosystem"` line observes an external ecosystem's own changes and runs from its own state directory.

## How is daily-research scheduled and run?

Scheduling is defined by one `launchd` plist: `com.*.daily-research.plist` triggers `scripts/daily-research.sh` at 05:00. The script unsets `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (Max plan, not per-token billing) and `CLAUDECODE` (so it also runs from inside a Claude Code session), takes an atomic `mkdir` lock (`.daily-research.lock/` with a `pid` file; a dead-PID lock is stolen), runs a real OAuth probe (a cheap Haiku call — `claude --version` cannot detect expiry), fail-fasts on a legacy config schema, then runs `rotation-pick` and the per-line calls. Every `claude -p` call redirects stdin with `< /dev/null` to prevent MCP stdio conflicts. Logs rotate after 30 days; macOS notifications report success, failure, auth errors, and lint hard fails. After the lines, a vault-side wiki ingest (Pass 3, non-fatal) and the metrics append run. Test seams: `DR_DATE`, `DR_ONLY_TRACK`, `DR_FORCE_TRACK`.

## What models does daily-research use and why?

Call 1 uses Claude Opus: rotation frees the daily budget for one high-quality explainer per line (ADR-0010). Call 2 uses the model named in `[verification] model`, Sonnet by default: verification and clarity are bounded editing tasks that benefit from a fresh context more than from peak reasoning (raise it to Opus if misses become visible). The auth probe is a minimal Claude Haiku call. Runs are invoked with `--append-system-prompt-file` to preserve Claude Code's default capabilities, `--allowedTools` for minimum privilege including path-scoped write access, `--disallowedTools` as a deny layer, `--output-format json` (fed to metrics), and `--no-session-persistence`.

## Is there a quality evaluation framework?

No LLM judge. An LLM-as-Judge framework once scored each report on 6 dimensions; it was suspended in 2026-02 for poor cost-to-value and removed on 2026-06-29. Evaluation is in-loop only (ADR-0010): the question screen and the verification + clarity pass consume their verdicts inside the same run; the only thing stored is the verification tally (supported / partial / unsupported / unverifiable), which counts sentences against their sources rather than scoring a report. Structure governs the rest — the citation gate, the deterministic ctl-016 lint, the ctl-015 gate — while the *content* of each note is judged by the human reader and the weekly `/dr-review` (ADR-0006). A post-hoc LLM judge is explicitly not to be revived.

## Who is shimo4228?

shimo4228 (shimomoto-tatsuya) is the author of daily-research. The author's hub, https://github.com/shimo4228/shimo4228, lists the author's practice lines (long-running, independently citable projects) with their concept DOIs; daily-research maps five DOI-registered repos as lines — the Agent Knowledge Cycle (AKC, 10.5281/zenodo.19200726), the Contemplative Agent (10.5281/zenodo.19212118), Agent Attribution Practice (AAP, 10.5281/zenodo.19652013), authorship-strategy (10.5281/zenodo.20263316), and attention-not-self (10.5281/zenodo.20262112) — plus the observation repos desire-frontier and edge-frontier. It is a companion engine rather than part of any single research line, and it is the *write* side of a human-mediated knowledge cycle: notes land in a shared vault wiki, and each research line folds findings back into its own repo by hand (ADR-0003).

## Glossary: what do the core terms mean?

- **Line (track)** is defined as a named research stream in `config.toml`. A line with `mode = "repo"` (the default, and the form `mode` may be omitted for) maps 1:1 to a research repository via `[[tracks.<line>.repos]]`, and the repo's directory becomes the run's cwd.
- **Ecosystem line** is defined as a line with `mode = "ecosystem"` (ADR-0018): it has no target repository and observes an external ecosystem's own changes — new OSS, tools, releases, design trends — rather than an external development relevant to a repo. Its call 1 runs with cwd = `state/<line>/`, `prompts/ecosystem-research-protocol.md`, and `--safe-mode`; the schema rejects `repos` and `context_files` on such a line. `jev` is the one configured today.
- **Rotation-pick** is defined as the deterministic, stateless selection of today's lines: a window of `lines_per_day` (K) consecutive lines starting at `date.toordinal() × K mod N` over the N rotating lines (cycle order = config order) plus every `daily = true` line.
- **Daily line** is defined as a line with `daily = true` that runs every morning outside the rotation cycle and is excluded from the rotation's N; `jev` is configured this way (ADR-0018).
- **Call 1 / Call 2** are defined as the per-line Opus research run and the fresh-context verification + clarity pass (clarity first as defect detection only, then every claim re-fetched and corrected against its source; fail-open, and a failed pass leaves the line `unverified`).
- **Explanatory report** is defined as the note format: one external development explained for a zero-context reader in prose with no fixed headings, `kind: article|brief` in the frontmatter, a deadline-only 機会メモ tail and a ソース section; no proposals.
- **Question-level dedup** is defined as the rule governing repeats: the same question with the same answer is not re-selected, the same question with new evidence may be updated, and the same topic under a different question is allowed; `past_topics.json` entries carry `question` and `answer_scope`.
- **Content state** is defined as one of `article`, `brief`, `quiet`, `hold` — the honest outcome a run declares in its run receipt, which the report-existence gate reads.
- **Run receipt / evidence file / verify.json** are defined as the three per-run files in `state/<line>/runs/`: `{date}.json` (the declared state), `{date}.md` (3–6 claims with source, locator, provenance, fetch_status), and `{date}.verify.json` (call 2's tally).
- **Expiry condition (失効条件)** is defined as the valid-until date every 機会メモ entry must carry; knowledge in the LLM space goes stale on a one-week scale, so every claim also carries an as-of date.
- **Diff-first** is defined as the rule that watched sources are checked only for changes since last-seen; re-surveying answered questions is forbidden.
- **Watched sources / playbook / brief / pending** are defined as the per-line state files in `state/<line>/`: `watched-sources.md` (sources + last-seen; on an ecosystem line the same file holds the watchlist table 名前 / canonical URL / 種別 / 初出日 / last-attempt / last-seen / 最後に報告した意味のある変化 / 状態, where 状態 ∈ active / watch / hold / stalled / archived and entries are never deleted), `playbook.md` (dated situation→action entries, delta-updated only), `brief.md` (the line's subject and open questions, the short context a run starts from), and `pending.md` (held questions and opportunity memos with states pending / resolved / contradicted / expired / unverifiable).
- **Citation gate** is defined as the rule that every cited URL must have been resolved via WebFetch during the run.
- **Self-contamination guard** is defined as the rule that artifacts matching config `self_signals` (the operator's own work) never count as external signals.
- **ctl-015 / ctl-016** are defined as the receipt-driven per-line report-existence gate (→ OK / E_PARTIAL / E_NO_REPORT, where E_NO_REPORT means no line passed the gate) and the deterministic report lint (hard: ソース section and citations; soft: 機会メモ, source count, body length — the soft checks are skipped for `kind: brief`).
- **DR-Expect** is defined as a commit trailer `DR-Expect: <metric> <op> <value>` stating the expected effect of a change on `metrics.jsonl`, reconciled by `expect-check` during `/dr-review`.
- **Frozen archive** is defined as the status of `graph.jsonld` after ADR-0008: historical concept-cluster data, no further increments.

## Configure a line

Each `[tracks.X]` entry is a research **line** (the config and the `DR_*_TRACK` variables still say *track*) mapped to one research repository via a `[[tracks.X.repos]]` entry. The area of interest is the repo's own operational context, read at runtime from inside the repo.

```toml
[general]
vault_path = "/path/to/your/obsidian/vault"
output_dir = "daily-research"
lines_per_day = 3                                # how many lines run per morning (the rotation window)
# Self-contamination guard: artifacts matching these strings never count as
# "external signals" (third-party mentions/adoptions of them are fine)
self_signals = ["github.com/YOUR_GITHUB_HANDLE", "Your Name"]

[verification]
model = "sonnet"                                 # model for call 2 (verification + clarity)

[tracks.example_line]
name = "Research Line A 前進"
focus = "What this line is about (a description of the subject, not a selection criterion)"
aliases = ["old_track_a"]                        # legacy track names whose history keeps feeding dedup
context_files = [".notes/TASKS.md", "docs/manifesto.md"]  # repo-relative; read after the question is chosen (Step 3b); missing files are skipped
sources = ["arXiv / Semantic Scholar (your keywords)"]
# daily = true                                   # run every morning outside the rotation (ADR-0011)

[[tracks.example_line.repos]]
key = "repo_a"
target_repo = "/path/to/your/research-repo-a"    # becomes the run's cwd (read-only)
target_doi = "10.xxxx/zenodo.xxxxxxxx"           # optional

[tracks.example_ecosystem_line]                  # a line with no repo (ADR-0018)
name = "Example Ecosystem 観測"
mode = "ecosystem"                               # cwd = state/example_ecosystem_line, ecosystem protocol, --safe-mode
daily = true
template = "templates/report-template-ecosystem.md"
focus = "The ecosystem to watch, and what to look at in it"
sources = ["Official site / docs / GitHub org", "GitHub search, package registries"]
# no repos and no context_files — the schema rejects both for mode = "ecosystem"
```

Reports are generated in Japanese by default; change the language constraint in `prompts/repo-research-protocol.md` (and `prompts/ecosystem-research-protocol.md`). The prompts are written in Japanese. See [CONTRIB](docs/CONTRIB.md) for CLI flags and environment variables.

## Project structure

```
daily-research/
├── scripts/
│   ├── daily-research.sh       # Orchestrator (rotation-pick → per line: call 1 research + call 2 verification/clarity, cwd = the line's repo, or state/<line> for an ecosystem line)
│   ├── lib/                    # Sourced shell libraries + the Python parsing module
│   │   ├── env.sh log.sh notify.sh lock.sh auth.sh claude.sh
│   │   └── dr_pipeline.py      # Single stdlib-only JSON/TOML module (line-brief, past-themes, receipt-read, verify-read, report-lint, metrics)
│   ├── check-auth.sh           # Real OAuth probe health check (shares lib/auth.sh)
│   └── pre-commit.sh           # Secret / syntax guard
├── prompts/                    # repo-research-protocol.md + ecosystem-research-protocol.md (call 1) + verification-protocol.md (call 2)
├── templates/report-template*.md      # Explanatory-report writing rules + fixed tail sections (per-line overrides: edge, ecosystem)
├── state/                      # Per-line brief / pending / watched-sources / playbook / runs (gitignored)
├── graph.jsonld                # FROZEN archive of the retired concept-graph pipeline (docs/graph-schema.md)
├── config.example.toml         # Line → repo mapping (config.toml is gitignored)
├── tests/                      # bats (daily-research / e2e-mock / lib) + pytest (dr_pipeline_test.py)
└── docs/                       # RUNBOOK, CONTRIB, graph-schema, adr/
```

## Key design decisions

| Decision | Why |
|----------|-----|
| Per-repo in-context research: per picked line, call 1 = Opus research + call 2 = fresh-context verification and clarity revision (Sonnet by default), cwd = the repo | The central 2-pass concept-graph pipeline could only see repos through synced graphs, so selection degenerated into gap-filling surveys; the operational context that knows what to advance lives inside each repo ([ADR-0008](docs/adr/0008-per-repo-in-context-research.md)) |
| Objective = explain one external development and what it means for the repo, not concept reinforcement | Corroboration-as-theme is a benchmarked failure mode ([ADR-0008](docs/adr/0008-per-repo-in-context-research.md)); the proposal/approval framing turned every note into a pending to-do, so notes are now reading material with a deadline-only 機会メモ tail ([ADR-0009](docs/adr/0009-explanatory-report-and-brief-retirement.md)); the adversarial refutation framing was later retired for readability ([ADR-0014](docs/adr/0014-trend-explanation-report.md)) |
| Diff-first + citation gate baked into the run structure | Survey-per-run is a documented anti-pattern; sycophantic drift needs structural countermeasures, not prompt intent ([ADR-0008](docs/adr/0008-per-repo-in-context-research.md)) |
| Repos are read-only at three layers (doctrine / execution / permissions) | Contributions flow through vault notes a human folds back in, avoiding cross-repo pollution |
| Lines map to research repositories | Fixed topic domains caused structural saturation ([ADR-0001](docs/adr/0001-research-repo-feedback-engine.md)); 1:1 repo lines since [ADR-0007](docs/adr/0007-return-to-four-repo-concept-reinforcement.md); in the author's configuration as of 2026-10, seven repo lines, run three a morning as a rotation window ([ADR-0017](docs/adr/0017-three-line-window-content-states-and-verification-pass.md)) |
| A line may have no repo: `mode = "ecosystem"` | Some subjects are an outside ecosystem rather than a repo's surroundings, and forcing one into a repo line makes the repo's context the selection filter; an ecosystem line runs from its own state directory under its own call-1 protocol, with the shared receipt / gate / content-state contract unchanged. The daily `jev` line is the first one ([ADR-0018](docs/adr/0018-ecosystem-mode-and-daily-jev-line.md)) |
| Four content states with a receipt-driven gate, and source verification in call 2 | "A fresh topic at full length every morning" forces an article out of a morning with no material; an honest quiet or hold is a normal result, and the line's success is decided from its run receipt. The claims are checked by a process other than the writer, re-fetching each source ([ADR-0017](docs/adr/0017-three-line-window-content-states-and-verification-pass.md)) |
| Local state files, not external MCP memory | The previous Mem0 MCP integration ran zero times for 32 days due to silent failure; a local file fails loudly |
| Shell orchestration + stdlib Python parser | No pip dependencies at runtime; JSON/TOML parsing lives in one testable `dr_pipeline.py` module |

Operational rationale (real auth probe vs `--version`, `--append-system-prompt-file`, path-scoped `--allowedTools`, `--max-turns`, `< /dev/null` stdin redirect) lives in [CONTRIB](docs/CONTRIB.md). In the author's own use, daily-research is also the *write* side of a knowledge cycle shared across several research lines: observed architecture, not a roadmap ([ADR-0003](docs/adr/0003-cross-line-knowledge-cycle.md)). The self-improvement loop (a per-line check that the line's report exists, a deterministic lint of the note's fixed sections, a daily record in `metrics.jsonl`, expected effects written into commits and checked against that record, and a roughly weekly review by the author) is preserved from [ADR-0006](docs/adr/0006-self-improvement-loop-human-consumer.md): no score is kept for an automated judge, and whether the notes are good is left to the person who reads them.

## Gotchas

- **Runs from inside a Claude Code session too**: `lib/env.sh` unsets `CLAUDECODE`, so the nested-session check passes (verified 2026-08-22). Test seams: `DR_FORCE_TRACK=<line>` (one line, even outside today's window), `DR_ONLY_TRACK=<line>` (only that line among today's picks), `DR_DATE=YYYY-MM-DD`.
- **OAuth token expires ~4 days** (the author's observation, recorded 2026-06-21): refresh by running `claude` interactively. The real auth probe (a one-turn Haiku call, not `claude --version`, which passes with an expired token) stops the run before any line and sends a re-auth notification.
- **Claude Code plugins cause hangs**: globally-installed plugins initialize their MCP servers on every `claude -p` call (the author's observation, recorded 2026-06-21). Disable them per-project in `.claude/settings.json` (see [RUNBOOK](docs/RUNBOOK.md)).
- **launchd doesn't source `.zshrc`**: all PATH entries must be explicit in the script and plist.
